name: Brunei Darussalam
headline: Brunei Darussalam: +1.0% growth in 2025, −0.3% inflation, debt 2% of GDP
sections: Brunei Darussalam is a $15.0 billion economy (2025), the world's 149th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +1.0% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $92K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 9.9% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose −0.3% in 2025, in deflation, down from 3.7% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 4.7% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 18.2% (2025).
Gross government debt is 2% of GDP (2025), a low level. The general government balance is −17.7% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is +18.0% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 124% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 0.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 1% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 75.5 years (2024). Population: 460 thousand (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
